full_text_en:
Ma Qing et al. v. Nanjing Grand Metro Hotel Co., Ltd. et al. — Dispute over Personal Injury Compensation

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to Article 6 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases concerning Personal Injury Compensation*, a party with a safety guarantee obligation shall perform such obligation within a reasonable scope, which shall be determined based on common sense. Where the party with the safety guarantee obligation has fulfilled such obligation, and a person with full capacity for civil conduct suffers damage due to his or her own misjudgment, the consequences shall be borne by the actor himself or herself.

Plaintiffs:
Ma Qing, female, 82 years old, residing at Heping New Village, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Qian Nanyan, female, 32 years old, residing at Ningxia Road, Gulou District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Qian Nanpeng, male, 29 years old, residing at Heping New Village, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

Defendants:
Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, domiciled at Xuanwumen, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Xiao Gao, Director of the Exhibition Hall.
Nanjing Grand Metro Mingji Hotel Co., Ltd., domiciled at Xuanwumen, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Wu Haiming, Chairman of the Company.
Xintai Securities Co., Ltd., Nanjing Xuanwumen Securities Business Department, domiciled at Xuanwumen, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Person in Charge: Huang Bo, General Manager of the Business Department.
Xintai Securities Co., Ltd., domiciled at Changjiang Road, Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.
Legal Representative: Qian Kaifa, Chairman of the Company.

Plaintiffs Ma Qing, Qian Nanyan, and Qian Nanpeng filed an action with the Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, Jiangsu Province, against Defendants Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, Nanjing Grand Metro Mingji Hotel Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Grand Metro Hotel"), Xintai Securities Co., Ltd., Nanjing Xuanwumen Securities Business Department (hereinafter "Xintai Securities Business Department"), and Xintai Securities Co., Ltd. (hereinafter "Xintai Securities Company") regarding a dispute over personal injury compensation.

The Plaintiffs Ma Qing, Qian Nanyan, and Qian Nanpeng alleged: The Defendant Xintai Securities Business Department had set up a VIP trading room in Room 207, 2nd Floor, No. 22 Xuanwumen, Xuanwu District, Nanjing (hereinafter "Room 207"). While the Plaintiffs' relative Qian Jin was trading stocks in this room, he went onto an outdoor platform to retrieve an insole that had fallen there. Because the platform floor suddenly collapsed, Qian Jin fell to his death. Post-accident investigation revealed that although the platform appeared identical to balconies in all other respects, its base was merely a thin layer of plasterboard with no load-bearing capacity, and no warning was posted forbidding entry onto the platform. As the owner and operator of the accident premises, Defendants Jiangsu Exhibition Hall, Grand Metro Hotel, Xintai Securities Company, and Xintai Securities Business Department failed to give adequate warning and take preventive measures regarding the platform's serious safety hazard, and therefore should all bear corresponding civil liability for Qian Jin's death. The Plaintiffs requested that the four Defendants be ordered to jointly and severally pay to the Plaintiffs compensation for death in the amount of RMB 232,040, living expenses for dependents in the amount of RMB 10,437.50, funeral expenses in the amount of RMB 11,090, and moral damages in the amount of RMB 50,000, totaling RMB 303,567.50.

Defendant Jiangsu Exhibition Hall argued: We only constructed the framework of the accident building; the other parts were decorated and invested by Defendant Grand Metro Hotel. We were not at fault regarding Qian Jin's death. The Plaintiffs' request that we bear civil liability has no legal basis, and their claims should be rejected.

Defendant Grand Metro Hotel argued: After the accident building was completed, pursuant to the local government's requirements for comprehensive environmental improvement in the area, we installed platforms on the exterior wall of the building to place air conditioner outdoor units. To prevent accidents, we installed restrictors on every window in the building, limiting the ability of persons inside to open windows and mistakenly enter these platforms. Even workers performing tasks on these platforms must have protective auxiliary measures. Qian Jin, using tools, privately damaged the restrictor on the window, opened the window, and entered the platform outside the window of Room 207, resulting in his fall to death. We have already fulfilled our safety guarantee obligation and should not be held liable for Qian Jin's death. The Plaintiffs' claims against us should be dismissed.

Defendants Xintai Securities Business Department and Xintai Securities Company argued: Our company started leasing the first and second floors of the Grand Metro Hotel in late July 2005 to establish a securities business premises. At that time, platforms for placing air conditioner outdoor units already existed on the exterior wall of the building; these were not "balconies" as claimed by the Plaintiffs. Qian Jin, ignoring the danger of climbing out the window, privately used a screwdriver to unscrew the restrictor on the window of Room 207 and climbed out, resulting in his accidental death. Qian Jin was a person with full capacity for civil conduct and should be responsible for his own actions. Qian Jin died after falling from the premises during his activities in our business department. We deeply sympathize with this and, out of humanitarian considerations, have already lent RMB 8,000 to Plaintiff Qian Nanpeng to handle Qian Jin's funeral. However, for our company, this accident was unforeseeable and unpreventable. We have fulfilled our safety guarantee obligation within a reasonable scope and therefore should not bear liability for Qian Jin's death. The Plaintiffs' claims against us should be dismissed.

After accepting the case, the Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing, on its own authority, obtained from the Xuanwumen Police Station of the Nanjing Public Security Bureau photos taken by the police station related to the case, and records of inquiries with witnesses Cheng Jiamei, Wang Liqun, and Hou Guangsheng. The photos showed that the window of Room 207 was equipped with a restrictor, and a screwdriver was left on the windowsill. Witness Cheng Jiamei stated that on the day of the incident, he, Qian Jin, and Wang Liqun, three persons in total, were trading stocks in Room 207; he saw Qian Jin standing outside the window, holding onto the outer window frame, moving slowly on the windowsill facing inward, and after a while, when he looked again, the person had fallen; he and Wang Liqun went to the window and saw a hole in the platform, and a person lying on the ground on the first basement level below the platform, identified by clothing as Qian Jin. Witness Wang Liqun stated that at around 10 a.m. on that day, while watching stocks in Room 207, he suddenly heard a scream from outside; looking out the window, he saw someone lying below; there was a screwdriver on the windowsill, which had not been there the previous day and should have been brought by Qian Jin; he had opened this window before, and it could not be opened wide enough for a person to go out. Witness Hou Guangsheng stated that in the morning of that day, he passed by the securities company and saw a person on a platform on the second floor outside, and then saw that person fall from the platform.

The Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing found through trial:

The building at No. 22 Xuanwumen, Xuanwu District, Nanjing, was owned by Defendant Jiangsu Exhibition Hall and leased by Defendant Grand Metro Hotel. The window of Room 207 on the second floor was equipped with a restrictor, and an air conditioner outdoor unit was installed outside the window. There was a platform below the air conditioner outdoor unit. The window and the platform outside the window were both constructed and installed by Grand Metro Hotel. On July 22, 2005, Jiangsu Exhibition Hall as the property owner, Grand Metro Hotel as the property lessor, and Defendant Xintai Securities Company's branch, Defendant Xintai Securities Business Department, as the lessee, signed a "House Lease Agreement," stipulating that Xintai Securities Business Department would lease part of the first floor and the entire second floor of the building as premises for conducting securities business, for a lease term from July 21, 2005 to September 21, 2007.

On November 1, 2005, Qian Jin (son of Plaintiff Ma Qing and father of Plaintiffs Qian Nanyan and Qian Nanpeng) was trading stocks in Room 207 of Defendant Xintai Securities Business Department. At around 10 a.m., because an insole that had been placed on the windowsill to air fell onto the platform outside the window, Qian Jin removed the restrictor on the window of Room 207, climbed out the window onto the platform to retrieve the insole, and fell due to the collapse of the platform floor. He died after emergency medical treatment failed.

After the incident, Defendant Xintai Securities Business Department lent RMB 8,000 to Plaintiff Qian Nanpeng on November 5, 2005, to handle Qian Jin's funeral, and stated that the handling of the loan would be discussed separately after the funeral was completed.

The above facts were confirmed by the police report and photos provided by the Plaintiffs, the "House Lease Agreement" and photos provided by Defendant Grand Metro Hotel, the loan receipt and photos provided by Defendant Xintai Securities Company, the photos and inquiry records obtained by the court, and the statements of both parties during court proceedings.

The issues in dispute in this case were: 1. Whether the platform outside Room 207 was a balcony; 2. Whether each Defendant should bear civil liability for Qian Jin's death.

The Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing held:

I. A building balcony is a platform connecting indoor and outdoor spaces, on which people can step, enjoy the cool, sunbathe, or look into the distance. Because a balcony must have such functions, rooms with balconies in a building necessarily have doors leading to the balcony. Only through a door can people normally reach a balcony and engage in activities on it. The facts of this case proved that although there was a platform outside Room 207, there was no door leading to it; the platform could only be seen from the window. Therefore, this platform was not a balcony for people to engage in activities. The Plaintiffs' characterization of the platform outside Room 207 as a balcony was not accepted.

II. Article 126 of the *General Principles of the Civil Law* provides that if a building or structure collapses and causes damage to others, the owner or manager of the building or structure shall bear civil liability, unless they can prove that they were not at fault. Article 18 of the *Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests* provides: "Business operators shall ensure that the commodities or services they provide meet the requirements for the protection of personal and property safety." Article 6 of the *Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases concerning Personal Injury Compensation* also provides: "Where a natural person, legal person, or other organization engaged in business activities such as accommodation, catering, entertainment, or other social activities fails to fulfill its safety guarantee obligation within a reasonable scope, thereby causing personal injury to others, and the right holder for compensation requests it to bear corresponding compensation liability, the People's Court shall support such request." According to the above provisions, the owner or manager of a building shall ensure the safe use of the building. For damage caused to others by a collapse of the building, the owner or manager of the building can be exempted from liability only if they prove that they were not at fault. An operator conducting business activities within the building bears a safety guarantee obligation towards the public receiving its services therein. If the operator fails to fulfill its safety guarantee obligation, causing personal injury to others, it shall bear corresponding compensation liability. However, the operator only performs the safety guarantee obligation within a reasonable scope, which shall be determined based on common sense.

When Defendant Grand Metro Hotel decorated the building at No. 22 Xuanwumen, Nanjing, for aesthetic reasons and pursuant to the local government's requirements for comprehensive environmental improvement, it built platforms near the windows on the exterior wall of the building for placing air conditioner outdoor units. A person with full capacity for civil conduct should realize, from the fact that there was no door from indoors leading to the platform, that the platform outside the window was not a balcony. Considering that windows are not pedestrian passages, but to avoid persons unfamiliar with the situation from climbing over the windows to reach platforms without load-bearing capacity, Grand Metro Hotel also installed restrictors on the windows, limiting the extent to which the windows could be opened, so that persons could not enter or exit through the windows. This objectively eliminated the possibility of persons inside climbing over the windows to reach the platform. After Defendant Xintai Securities Business Department leased the premises as its business premises, it retained the restrictors installed on the windows. Qian Jin, based on his own misjudgment of the nature of the platform, used a screwdriver he had brought to privately remove the restrictor on the window of Room 207, climbed over the window to the platform outside, and fell to his death. Both Defendant Jiangsu Exhibition Hall and Grand Metro Hotel proved through the facts that, as the owner and manager of the building, they had ensured the safe use of the building and were not at fault for Qian Jin's fall to death. Both Defendant Xintai Securities Company and Xintai Securities Business Department also proved through the facts that they had fulfilled their safety guarantee obligation within a reasonable scope and should not be held liable for Qian Jin's fall to death. In fact, it was not that the owner or manager of the building failed to eliminate the safety hazard of the platform outside the window of Room 207, nor that the operator conducting business activities within the building failed to fulfill its safety guarantee obligation; rather, it was Qian Jin himself who destroyed the safety protection facility installed by the manager, thereby placing himself in a dangerous situation. As a person with full capacity for civil conduct, Qian Jin should bear the consequences of his own fault. Where restrictors had already been installed on the windows, requiring the owner, manager, or operator conducting business activities within the building to foresee that a person inside would use tools to unscrew the restrictor and climb over the window, and thus to issue a danger warning to such a person, exceeds the normal level of cognition and goes beyond the reasonable scope of fulfilling the safety guarantee obligation.

In summary, the Plaintiffs' claim that the Defendants failed to fulfill their safety guarantee obligation and should bear joint and several liability for Qian Jin's fall to death had no factual or legal basis and was not supported. Accordingly, the Xuanwu District People's Court of Nanjing rendered the following judgment on May 15, 2006:

The claims of Plaintiffs Ma Qing, Qian Nanyan, and Qian Nanpeng were dismissed.

Court costs of RMB 2,060 were borne by Plaintiffs Ma Qing, Qian Nanyan, and Qian Nanpeng.

Ma Qing, Qian Nanpeng, and Qian Nanyan, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, arguing: There was a seemingly sturdy platform outside the window of Room 207. The Appellees Grand Metro Hotel, Xintai Securities Company, and Xintai Securities Business Department had a duty to warn people not to engage in activities on that platform. Grand Metro Hotel, Xintai Securities Company, and Xintai Securities Business Department failed to fulfill this duty and should bear corresponding liability for the consequences of Qian Jin's fall to death.

The Appellees Grand Metro Hotel, Xintai Securities Company, and Xintai Securities Business Department agreed with the first-instance judgment in their defenses.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court, after trial, confirmed the facts found by the first-instance court.

The Nanjing Intermediate People's Court held:

The Appellee Grand Metro Hotel, as the lessor and manager of the premises in question, and the Appellees Xintai Securities Company and Xintai Xuanwumen Business Department, as operators conducting securities business within the premises, could only fulfill their safety guarantee obligation within a reasonable scope. There was no door leading to the platform inside the premises. An ordinary person should thus be able to determine that the platform outside the window was not meant for entry. Additionally, the window of Room 207 had a restrictor limiting the extent to which the window could be opened. Under normal circumstances, it was impossible for a person to reach the platform through the window. Based on the normal level of cognition, neither Grand Metro Hotel nor Xintai Securities Company or Xintai Securities Business Department could foresee that a person inside would use tools to remove the restrictor and climb out the window to the platform. Therefore, requiring Grand Metro Hotel, Xintai Securities Company, and Xintai Securities Business Department to give further warning of the danger of the platform outside the window of Room 207 exceeded the reasonable scope of the safety guarantee obligation. The first-instance court's findings were clear and the application of law was appropriate, and the judgment should be affirmed. The Appellants' grounds for appeal were untenable and should be rejected. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1(1) of the *Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, the Nanjing Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on July 31, 2006:

The appeal was dismissed and the original judgment was affirmed.
